
Two arXiv papers from the RSS feed meet ≥3 inclusion criteria with high confidence: one on generalizable tool-calling in agentic systems, and one on context/state management for long-horizon agent tasks. Grok social signals were low-quality (no social evidence, some URLs unverifiable) and are excluded.

## Suggestions

- [MAVEN: Improving Generalization in Agentic Tool Calling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30738) — Proposes MAVEN, a framework for improving generalization in agentic tool calling, addressing tool-use design, execution reliability, and empirical evaluation across diverse agentic tasks.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)

- [Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30785) — Presents a context management framework designed for long-horizon agentic tasks, addressing state management, execution-time context adaptation, and iterative refinement across extended agent trajectories.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability)
